prompt: Convert the landing page in ./source (index.html, style.css, script.js, images/) into a WordPress block theme.
- Theme name: Northstar, slug and text domain: northstar, author: Northstar, Inc.
- This is a non-interactive run, so do not ask questions: state your assumptions briefly and use sensible defaults.

steps.text: Starting: I'll read the source and the plugin's reference docs.

steps.name: Bash
items: ls -R source | head -50 && wc -c source/* && R=${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/references && ls $R && wc -

steps.text: Status: I've read the source and the plugin's rules, and I know what the doctor checks. I'm now writing the theme files, starting with `theme.json`, the PHP, and the assets.

I converted the landing page into the Northstar block theme at `./northstar-theme/`, and the doctor passes. I haven't run it in a live WordPress install. The doctor can't check how it looks, so the Site Editor and visual match still need a manual pass.

I also rendered every pattern through PHP. The block-comment JSON is valid and the blocks are balanced. `Overall: 5/5 scripts passed.`

## What was built
`index.html` became a front page made of seven editable patterns: hero, features, stats, testimonials, pricing, FAQ and call to action. The header and footer are template parts that load their own patterns.

I also added the standard fallback templates: `index`, `home`, `single`, `page`, `archive`, `search` and `404`. The images are in `assets/images/`. The theme has no WooCommerce and no build tooling.

## Assumptions
- **Colors and sizes:** the palette, font sizes and spacing come from the source `:root` variables. The system font stack is kept, so no font files are bundled.
- **Mobile menu:** `script.js` is dropped. The core Navigation block's mobile menu replaces it, so the theme ships no JavaScript.
- **FAQ:** the FAQ uses the native Details block.
- **Site title:** the brand name in the header and footer is the Site Title block. Set it to "Northstar" in Settings → General, or the header will show whatever the site is named.
- **Skip link:** it lives in the header pattern, and I removed core's duplicate skip link.
- **Copyright year:** it is generated, not hardcoded.
- **Contrast fix:** I made one deliberate change to the source colors. The copyright text moved from `#64748b` to `#94a3b8`, because the original failed 4.5:1 contrast on the dark footer.
- **Menu links:** header and footer menu links point to `/#section`, so they work from non-home pages too.
- **Not included:** I left out comments templates and style variations, which a single landing page doesn't need.
- **Tested up to:** `Tested up to` is 7.0, from the plugin's defaults. I didn't confirm it against the current WordPress release.

## Install
1. Zip the `northstar-theme/` folder.
2. Upload it in Appearance → Themes → Add New → Upload Theme, then activate.
3. Check that the templates appear in Site Editor → Templates.

There is no `npm` step.

## Before you ship
- [ ] Set the Site Title to "Northstar".
- [ ] Replace the placeholder `screenshot.png` (a solid indigo 1200×900 image) with a real screenshot.
- [ ] Check the page side by side with `source/index.html` at desktop and mobile widths. Also confirm the sticky header and the hero gradient.
- [ ] Open the front page in the Site Editor and confirm no block shows a validation warning.
- [ ] Run Lighthouse and a `WP_DEBUG` pass.
